set: 2026-07-30 (seeded by hand from a measured GREEN run: guards.ps1 exit 0, board comparison-2026-07-30.json)
readme: The accepted high-water coverage mark for every instrumented check. audit-coverage-ledger.ps1 compares out/coverage-ledger.json against this and reports a check that examined materially fewer rows than it used to. Move it with 'audit-coverage-ledger.ps1 -Accept' ONLY after you know why a number shrank. Every 'examined' below was read off the real run, never estimated. 'tolerance' is the fraction the number may fall before it is a finding; the default is 0.10, which was chosen by measuring the day-over-day change in the board's priced-cell count across all 18 retained boards (worst drop in the whole history -5.0%, worst drop since 2026-07-18 -0.7%), so 0.10 produces ZERO findings on real history. A wider tolerance below always says why. 'phase' is the job that writes the row - publish (guards.ps1) or cycle (check-ad-cycles.ps1) - and a missing row is only a finding in its own phase, so a fresh cloud checkout with an empty out/ does not report every cycle check as missing.

audit-food-category.why: priced cells scanned for a wrong-CLASS product (the blueberries-as-Bai-beverage guard). Measured 2026-07-30: 2663 scanned of 3196 priced cells, 372 skipped because their commodity's category maps to no class list and 161 because the cell carries no product name. Board-derived, so the measured 0.10 band applies. A later same-day board rebuild read 2661 of 3194, well inside the band.

guards/3-pin-derivable.why: override pins re-derived from their own verified link. Small N and the pin SET is regenerated by generate-board-overrides, so it moves by whole pins (16 earlier today, 19 now); a narrow band here would cry wolf on ordinary pin churn. The founding failure is a 100% drop, which BLIND catches regardless of tolerance.

guards/3-pin-identity.why: pins whose link was product-identity-checked by audit-name-drift. THE FOUNDING BUG: this was 0 of 16 while the ok line beside it said 16 checked, because name-drift read only the staple board and every pin is a recipe-board id. Today 9 of 19 - the other 10 have no board .item to compare against. Same small-N reasoning as above.

guards/4-factor.why: board cells compared against their own linked product's per-unit. The single largest coverage number on the publish path and the one most directly tied to the board, so the measured 0.10 band applies.

guards/5-multipack.why: rows this guard formed a multipack VERDICT about. THE RATCHET IS DELIBERATELY OFF HERE (tolerance 1.0), and that was measured rather than assumed: guards.ps1's own note at invariant 5 records this number as 0 for every newest-Walmart file from 2026-07-05 to 07-14 and 121 on 2026-07-23, against 380 today. At tolerance 0.5 a return to 121 is a 68.2% drop and fires REGRESSED on a value the code beside it documents as normal - verified by running the auditor against a 121 ledger. The count depends entirely on how verbosely the current Walmart capture writes pack counts into names, so it is not ratchetable from one observation. The founding failure here is a 100% drop, which BLIND catches at any tolerance. Narrow this only once a few weeks of ledger show a real distribution.

guards/6-collapse.why: stores compared against their own capture history. 6 of 7 today; sams is the one that cannot be evaluated (a single out/regular capture, so no history).

guards/9-freshness.why: stores that completed a freshness note. Guard 10's own header names guard 9 as the ONLY staleness watch on Baker's, Fareway, Sam's and Walmart, so a store dropping out of this count is a store with no clock at all.

guards/10-store-charges.why: rows where what we publish was verified against the store's own current_price - the ONLY check comparing our number to the store's. Wide band because the denominator is the engine's 14-day Walmart union plus every other store's newest capture, so it steps down whenever a capture ages out of the window. I have exactly ONE measurement of it (24018 on 2026-07-30) and will not pretend to a distribution I did not measure; narrow this once a few days of ledger exist.

guards/11-bakers-provenance.why: Baker's rows whose provenance was checked. THE FOUNDING BUG OF THIS WHOLE COMPONENT: the old guard 11 filtered on .upc and source_ad='bakersplus', Baker's moved to the Kroger API, and it printed ok over 0 of 6,960 rows for FIVE DAYS on the board's largest store. Band set to 0.25 because the row count is whatever the day's API pull returned; a total collapse is caught by BLIND at any tolerance.

audit-ff-carry.why: empty Family Fare search terms re-probed against Freshop. THE RATCHET IS DELIBERATELY OFF HERE (tolerance 1.0): this number FALLS when the FF pull gets BETTER, so ratcheting it would fire a finding every time somebody fixed the thing it watches. The row exists for NEVER-RECORDED and STALE, which is the failure that actually happened - the script threw on its own report line before printing anything and 'ff-carry' appears 0 times in 2,716 lines of ad-cycle-log.txt, so for 17 days there was no output to be suspicious of. max_age_days is 3 rather than 2 because it runs on the ad cycle, not on every publish. NOTE: nothing yet runs the ratchet with -Phase cycle, so those two verdicts fire only on a manual run until check-ad-cycles.ps1 gets its own hook.
